title: Interception of Registration Data
description: Sensitive data (email, password, government ID) transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by attackers during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted without encryption or with weak encryption.

title: Direct Identification via Transmitted Identifiers
description: Name and government ID in transit allow direct identification of the parent user if intercepted.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are transmitted in plaintext or with insufficient protection.

title: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Data
description: Authentication service may store passwords or government IDs without proper security measures, leading to unauthorized access or misuse.
assumptions: Assumes the service does not implement secure storage practices (e.g., hashing passwords, encrypting IDs).

title: Non-compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Transmission of sensitive data without encryption may violate GDPR or similar data protection regulations.
assumptions: Assumes applicable regulations require encryption of data in transit.

title: Unnecessary user data disclosure
description: Authentication Service shares user data beyond what is required for parent authentication, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: User data includes sensitive information not strictly needed for the parent's role.
uncertainty_note: Assumes user data exceeds minimal necessary scope; context-dependent.

title: Unencrypted data in transit
description: JWT and user data transmitted without encryption, risking interception by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Transport layer security (e.g., TLS) is not enforced for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Depends on implementation; if TLS is used, this threat may not apply.

title: Insecure data storage by parent
description: Parent User may store received JWT/user data without adequate security controls, enabling potential misuse.
assumptions: Parent lacks secure storage practices for sensitive authentication data.
uncertainty_note: Assumes parent's storage practices are not audited or secured.

title: Interception of parent credentials during transmission
description: Parent's email and password sent over the network could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Network communication is not encrypted or uses weak encryption.

title: Insecure storage of parent credentials
description: Authentication service may store parent's password without encryption, risking exposure if the database is compromised.
assumptions: Service stores credentials in plaintext or with weak hashing.

title: Linking child's account to parent's identity
description: Using parent's email for child's login creates a link between the child's activities and the parent's identity, potentially exposing the parent's data.
assumptions: Parent's email is used as a unique identifier for the child's account.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Sensitive child data (name, DOB, govt ID) transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without encryption.
uncertainty_note: Assuming no encryption is used; if TLS is in place, likelihood may be lower.

title: Unauthorized Data Usage Beyond Profile Management
description: Child profile data may be used for purposes other than intended profile management, such as marketing or third-party sharing.
assumptions: P3 lacks strict access controls or data usage policies.
uncertainty_note: Depends on organizational policies not specified in the DFD.

title: Child Data Enables Individual Identification
description: Stored child profile data (name, DOB, govt ID) can be used to uniquely identify the child, increasing privacy risks.
assumptions: Data is stored in a retrievable format without pseudonymization.

title: Mandatory Collection of Sensitive Government ID
description: Requiring government ID for child profile creation may violate data minimization principles under privacy regulations.
assumptions: Govt ID is not necessary for the stated purpose of profile management.
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdictional legal requirements not specified.

title: Child Data Linked with Other Datasets
description: Child profile data could be linked with other internal or external datasets, creating a comprehensive profile of the child.
assumptions: P3 has access to or shares data with other systems containing child-related information.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if data linking occurs; depends on system architecture.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Profiles
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB may be accessed by unauthorized parties if access controls are insufficient.

title: Data Used Beyond Consented Purposes
description: Stored child profiles may be used for purposes not originally intended or consented to by the child's guardians.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Data Protection Laws
description: Storing child profiles may violate regulations such as COPPA or GDPR if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Child profile data transmitted between P3 and DS2 may be intercepted if not encrypted.

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Profile Modifications
description: Updates to child profiles may not be logged, preventing accountability and non-repudiation.

title: Processing child data without valid consent
description: Video Management Service processes child's data without obtaining necessary parental consent, violating legal requirements like COPPA or GDPR-K.

title: Unencrypted data in transit
description: Video search and interaction data transmitted without encryption, risking interception and exposure.

title: Linking user actions to profile
description: Service correlates search, like, and comment data to build a detailed user profile, enabling tracking across sessions.

title: Data used beyond original purpose
description: Child's interaction data used for targeted advertising or third-party sharing without explicit consent.

title: Exposure of child's identity through comments
description: Comments may contain personally identifiable information, leading to direct identification of the child user.

title: Lack of transparency in data processing
description: Child and parents not adequately informed about how their data is collected and used by the service.

title: Direct identification of child via profile data
description: Child profile data sent to the datastore includes unique identifiers (e.g., child ID), enabling direct identification of the child.
assumptions: Process P3 transmits identifiable child data without anonymization.

title: Unencrypted data transmission
description: Child search and watch history is transmitted without encryption, risking interception and exposure.
assumptions: Data flow DF10 lacks encryption in transit.

title: Unauthorized secondary use of child data
description: Stored child profile data may be accessed or repurposed beyond original intent (e.g., marketing, third-party sharing).
assumptions: DataStore DS2 lacks strict access controls or usage policies.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection laws
description: Storing child search/watch history may violate regulations (e.g., COPPA) if consent and safeguards are inadequate.
assumptions: Process P3 does not implement required legal compliance measures.

title: Lack of transparency in data collection
description: Children/parents may not be informed about the collection and storage of their search and watch history.
assumptions: Process P3 does not provide clear privacy notices or consent mechanisms.

title: Child Identifiability via Uploaded Video
description: Parent uploads video containing child's identifiable information (e.g., face, voice), enabling direct identification of the child.

title: Video Interception During Upload
description: Unencrypted video transmission allows interception of sensitive content by unauthorized parties.

title: Metadata Linking Parent to Video
description: Upload metadata (e.g., timestamps, IP) links parent identity to video content, enabling correlation.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Video
description: Inadequate access controls on stored videos allow unauthorized viewing or extraction of sensitive data.

title: Video Use Beyond Parental Consent
description: Service repurposes uploaded videos for marketing or third-party sharing without explicit consent.

title: Parent Unaware of Data Processing
description: Parent lacks transparency about how uploaded videos are processed, stored, or shared by the service.

title: Linkability of child's viewing history
description: The Video Management Service logs which approved videos are streamed to each child, enabling linkage of viewing habits to the child's identity.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the service retains logs associating child IDs with video content.

title: Interception of video stream
description: Unencrypted video streams could be intercepted during transmission, exposing content to unauthorized parties.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether encryption is used in transit.

title: Insecure storage of video on child's device
description: If the child's device stores the video without adequate security, it could be accessed by unauthorized users.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the child's device lacks proper data protection measures.

title: Unauthorized disclosure by Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service may transmit government ID images to the File System without verifying user consent or proper authorization, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the Authentication Service lacks proper access controls or consent verification mechanisms.

title: Unencrypted transmission of government ID images
description: The data flow lacks encryption, allowing potential interception of sensitive government ID images during transmission between the Authentication Service and File System.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow does not implement transport-layer security (e.g., TLS).

title: Inadequate access controls on stored government ID images
description: The File System may not implement sufficient access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access stored government ID images.
assumptions: Assumes the File System lacks role-based access controls or encryption at rest.

title: JWT exposed via XSS leading to unauthorized access
description: Storing JWT in localStorage allows malicious scripts to access the token, enabling session hijacking and unauthorized data access.
assumptions: Assumes potential XSS vulnerabilities in the browser environment.

title: Unintended disclosure of child history data
description: Process P3 may share more child history data than necessary for parent review, leading to unintended disclosure of sensitive information.
assumptions: Data minimization controls are not enforced

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Child history data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.
assumptions: No encryption is used for data in transit

title: Data misuse by parent user
description: Parent may use child's history data for purposes beyond review, such as sharing with third parties or non-consensual profiling.
assumptions: No technical or policy controls restrict data usage post-receipt
